findings.body: On a clean Mac without cached sudo authorization, NONINTERACTIVE=1 prevents Homebrew from requesting the administrator password. The [Homebrew installer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh) uses sudo -n in this mode, so setup fails before installing the tools. Authenticate through the terminal during the promised curl | bash invocation and explain how to recover if authorization fails.
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — Homebrew bootstrap

findings.body: Installing uv through winget does not add uv's tool executable directory to PATH. On a fresh Windows account, Forge installs but the final forge --version cannot find it. The Mac script's export at scripts/install-mac.sh:63 lasts only inside the piped Bash process, leaving Forge unavailable afterward. Configure the tool directory persistently, expose it during setup, and explain any shell restart needed. [uv documents update-shell as the separate PATH configuration step](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/tools/#installing-tools).
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — Forge command availability

findings.body: The promised irm | iex invocation can run under Windows PowerShell's default Restricted policy, but npm resolves to npm.ps1 and is blocked, stopping setup before Claude Code installs. The npx invocation at line 82 has the same defect. Call npm.cmd and npx.cmd explicitly. See the [Node reproduction and workaround](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62427) and [Microsoft's default execution policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-5.1).
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — Windows npm execution

findings.body: The fixture retains the host PATH while expecting GitHub CLI and uv to be missing. The Windows suite runs through .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23–35, where line 31 installs uv; the [Windows runner also includes GitHub CLI](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-Readme.md). Consequently, check mode skips gh and the assertion at line 87 fails. If execution reaches installation, it can select real uv instead of the stub. Isolate tool discovery while retaining only the system commands the harness requires, including across the script's PATH refresh.

findings.body: These assertions permit extra installer calls, so reinstalling already-present Git and Node would still pass. Neither platform exercises all-present tools or existing browsers; Homebrew is always present, and Windows always reports WSL2 ready, leaving both bootstrap paths untested. Windows also omits assertions for the uv, Claude Code, Codex and Playwright installer calls. Extend the script-entry-point tests to verify no installation for present tools, each missing installer exactly once, and the Homebrew and WSL2 authorization/restart paths.

findings.body: The supplied functional-check paragraph records observed Mac runs but only says the Windows test is routed through CI; it records no Windows execution or observed result. The amended contract requires recording the stubbed runs for both scripts. Run the isolated Windows check and install paths and record their outcomes, including the WSL2 guidance. Clean-laptop installations may remain with the owner after merge, as explicitly allowed here.

findings.body: Any directory matching each browser prefix is considered sufficient, including obsolete or incomplete browser installations. Check mode therefore reports nothing missing and setup skips installation even when the intended Playwright version cannot launch those browsers. scripts/install-windows.ps1:23 uses the same predicate. Validate the required revisions and executable files; [Playwright requires specific browser binaries for each version](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers).
findings.title: Check usable Playwright revisions before skipping installation
